title: Quarterly shift - 1:1 bullet journal and action log
content:
Purpose: quick, scannable prep for the leadership 1:1 block and a running action log. Goal = make the 1:1s focused (decisions + blockers) so weekly sync is execution not discovery.

High level framing (1 sentence):
- Q2 shift: trade smarter throughput for slightly higher unit latency where it reduces cost 12–18% for top enterprise workloads. Need leadership alignment and 2 concrete runway decisions this week.

Top priorities to surface in 1:1s (pick 2 each meeting):
- Dedicated capacity commit thresholds: propose lowering min-reserve for burst lanes to increase utilization (ask for green light on pilot with 2 customers).
- Private deployment compliance checklist: confirm timeline for SOC2 + EU DPA signoff; signal any blockers to legal.
- Optimize tooling rollout: A/B test of caching recommendations vs. manual tuning (need to decide A/B metric & duration).
- Customer escalations: brief on 3 customers with latency regressions; propose fallback routing + credits.

CEO / COO 1:1 bullets:
- Quick ask: approve pilot to change reserved capacity floor for burst lanes (expected $X savings, notes in Confluence link).
- Risk: sales feedback that variable pricing is confusing; need a messaging approach — ask for marketing + sales sync.
- Hire ask: approve headcount for one SRE and one Product Ops in Q2 (justification: Dedicated ramp + rollout support).
- Prep: have 2 slide bullets ready showing predicted cost delta and customer impact.

Head of Product 1:1 bullets:
- Rollouts: gating metrics for Optimize (quality regression tolerance window = 1% perf delta baseline).
- Evals: need decision on whether to add automatic regression rollback after 3 failing prompt sets.
- Ask: prioritize console observability UX fixes (token breakdown by route) — need timeline.

Engineering lead 1:1 bullets:
- Technical ask: confirm fallback model chaining order and a timeline for per-request routing policy flags.
- Blocker: quantization test suite failing on sequenceLen 4096 (stack trace + repro in linked PR).
- Ops: check autoscaling policy metrics; can we add latency SLO breach alert at 95th token latency?

Notes-to-self / framing lines (quick reads):
- Start each 1:1 with one metric + one unresolved question. Keeps executive time for decisions.
- If asked for numbers, offer 2-minute snapshot and follow with a one-pager in <24h.
- Do not introduce new initiatives in 1:1s unless approval already pre-signed.

Running action log (fast format: action — owner — due — status):
- Draft burst-lane pilot proposal — Avery Chen — 2026-03-17 — in_progress
- Build customer impact slides (2 slides) — Samira Ortiz — 2026-03-12 — todo
- Add autoscaling latency alert rule to SRE runbook — Liam Nguyen — 2026-03-14 — todo
- Draft messaging doc for variable pricing — Product Marketing — 2026-03-20 — todo
- SOC2 evidence collection kickoff — Legal — 2026-03-21 — todo

Follow-ups from last sync (capture + next step):
- Customer X regression: assigned to Solutions Eng to verify cache warm-up windows. Next: target fix for 2026-03-11.
- Dedicated capacity SLA: concierge docs updated; need signoff from Sales Ops (waiting).

Open questions to escalate (short):
- Do we accept a 10% latency increase for 15% cost savings for enterprise Tier A? (need CEO decision)
- Which metric will we use as the A/B primary for Optimize opt-in (token-cost-adjusted throughput vs. end-user latency)?

Quick reminders (personal):
- Keep 1:1s to 25 minutes: 10m metric/updates, 10m decisions, 5m actions
- Bring two specific asks — one tactical, one strategic.
- After each 1:1, tag action owners in Slack + add to this file within 24h.

Draft email snippets (for after the meeting):
- "Thanks — next steps: Samira to deliver slides by 3/12; Avery to circulate pilot doc by 3/17; Liam to implement alert by 3/14. I'll follow up Friday with a concise summary."

Misc scratch bits (to prune later):
- If pilot approves, need a short checklist for onboarding customers (billing toggle, routing policy, telemetry flags).
- Consider internal alpha with 1 non-prod team to validate end-to-end rollback flow.

References (short):
- Confluence: Pilot design + expected savings -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=482910
- Jira: RINF-2041 (pilot epic), RINF-1998 (latency regressions)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-configs/pull/87

Next edit: flesh out pilot doc with explicit success criteria (incorporate feedback from Samira).

— end of scratchpad —
